result.day: Day 03 — "Специфікація як контракт" (15.09.2026, FWDAYS Crash Course Agentic Engineering, deck pages 124–171). Theme: "задача, закрита з доказом" — definition of done written BEFORE the agent starts, enforced by gates with exit codes (pnpm check / pnpm spec:check), SDD via OpenSpec 1.13.0 (/opsx:propose → /opsx:apply → /opsx:archive).

agentsMd.structure: Day 3 does not show the whole AGENTS.md; it quotes two parts (slide 12, slide 36) and names its sections: (a) a 'trust level' paragraph (Trust level 3 inside an OpenSpec change / level 1 outside), (b) a 'Definition of done' section for a change (all tasks.md items [x] · change archived · ## Purpose of the archived spec read by a human · ends with pnpm check output, not the word 'done'), (c) a 'Boundaries' section with the privacy line about ~/.claude and ~/.codex. AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md are listed on slide 2 as part of the harness that 'moved as files' from days 1–2 together with .claude/settings.json (allow-list + hooks), .claude/hooks (protect-env, log-filter, log-action), .agent-log/, docs/session-notes.md and a CI check. The same product/stack/data constraints are duplicated in openspec/config.yaml `context:` so the agent sees them in every artifact (slide 19). Slide 36 explicitly says AGENTS.md lines are advice, not enforcement: 'Hooks примушують — AGENTS.md радить'.
exampleRules: Trust level 3 ("Agent") inside an OpenSpec change: implement that change's tasks.md end to end — edit the files it needs, run allow-listed commands — and finish with pnpm check output. (slide 12, verbatim)

Outside a change: trust level 1 ("Assistant") — propose, then wait for a human decision before changing more than one file or running anything that is not on the allow-list in .claude/settings.json. (slide 12, verbatim)
Never read the real ~/.claude or ~/.codex in code, tests or demos (slide 36, verbatim, AGENTS.md Boundaries)

Definition of done for a change (slides 5, 12, 24): усі пункти tasks.md — [x] · зміну заархівовано · ## Purpose архівної специфікації прочитала людина · закінчує виводом pnpm check, а не словом «готово»
Demotion without discussion (slide 12): 'вийшов за межі зміни — рівень 1' (left the change's scope → back to level 1)
antiPatterns: Agent declares 'готово, усі перевірки пройшли' in chat — criterion appears after the work and is written by the same party that did the work (slide 6, 15)
Vague checklist items closable by any code: «ціни моделей рахуються коректно», «невідомі моделі обробляються», «покрити ціни тестами» (slide 11)
Returning $0 for an unknown model instead of an explicit 'unpriced' marker — silently sums into totals, no test without a scenario catches it (slide 11)
[x] in tasks.md put by the one who did the work, green mark without a list of what was checked (slide 15)
Relying on AGENTS.md alone for enforcement in acceptEdits mode — 'правку поза зміною Claude Code не заблокує. Рівень 1 там — інструкція. Примус — allow-list і hooks' (slide 12)
Generated skill text containing bare `openspec` calls — agent executes it as instruction and may hit a different global version (slide 23)

result.staticVsDynamicContext: Day 3 does not use the literal words 'static vs dynamic' but draws the line repeatedly: STATIC/advisory context = AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md rules, openspec/config.yaml `context:` (seen by agent when creating ANY artifact) and `rules:` (injected into a specific artifact type — specs or tasks), generated skills (.claude/skills/openspec-*/SKILL.md) and commands (.claude/commands/opsx/*.md) — 'Skill — це контекст, який писали не ви' (slide 23: 204 bare openspec calls in 18 generated files; the agent will execute generated text as instruction). DYNAMIC/enforced context = .claude/settings.json allow-list and deny, hooks (protect-env, log-filter, log-action), gates with exit codes (pnpm check, pnpm spec:check, CI), and files the agent reads at run time (docs/session-notes.md, docs/intent.md, fixtures/claude/README.md with the correct numbers). Slide 12: 'Що з цього примус' — permission mode is acceptEdits all evening, so an edit outside the change is NOT blocked; level 1 is an instruction, enforcement is allow-list + hooks. Slide 36: the privacy rule lives in AGENTS.md and config.yaml context (agent sees it), but protect-env hook and deny only cover .env*, Read is allow-listed without path restriction — 'Чесно: сьогодні це правило, а не примус'. Slide 19: 'CONTEXT: — у кожен артефакт … RULES: — у конкретний артефакт'. Proof expected: config.yaml committed; generated skills rewritten by openspec-pin (idempotent, '18 file(s) rewritten, 204 bare call(s) -> pnpm exec openspec'); gate spec:check fails if a bare call returns (e.g. after `openspec update`). Slide 15 'Гейт ≠ статус': status is read by a human, a gate is read by a script and can say 'no' via exit code.

result.loopEngineering: Day 3's loop is 'agent iterates until the gate's exit code is 0, not until it says done' (slide 13: 'Агент ітерує, доки гейт не зелений, — а не доки не скаже «готово»'). Concrete mechanics: (1) pnpm check = `typecheck → lint → test → spec:check` (slide 26), one command with non-zero exit on failure — 'одна команда перевірки з ненульовим кодом при провалі — переказ поради з AI-native SDLC playbook, Stage 4 Test' (slide 13). (2) openspec/config.yaml rule for tasks: `- The last task is "Run pnpm check and quote its summary line"` — so every tasks.md ends with the gate and the agent must quote the summary line, e.g. `spec:check ok — specs: 1 · active changes: 0 · archived: 1` (slides 19, 26). (3) Second config.yaml rule (added with fixtures, slide 39): the FIRST task is the scenario tests that must be seen RED; without it the agent put tests last and each 'confirm it passes' — no red stage visible. (4) Red → green loop in /opsx:apply (slide 40): task 1.1 runs scenario tests against current parser → `Tests 3 failed | 14 passed (17)` with the exact 'obvious parser' numbers from fixtures/claude/README.md ('tests fell for the RIGHT reason'), then 'правило за правилом, доки не зелене' → `Tests 17 passed (17)` (slide 41). (5) The cycle itself is a loop with gates at each exit (slide 13): propose → `pnpm spec:check`; apply → `pnpm check`; archive → `pnpm spec:check` (+ validate --archived). (6) Goal is set by the change, not the prompt: 'межі — у сценаріях, кроки — у tasks.md, кінець — код виходу' (slide 12). (7) Budget as a loop boundary: output ≤ 60 000 tokens, ≤ $3 at list price written in docs/intent.md BEFORE apply, measured AFTER from the transcript (`result` events of claude -p); mismatch is recorded, not hidden (slides 14, 37, 41). Honest limitation: in interactive Claude Code there is no per-task token limit; `--max-budget-usd <amount>` 'only works with --print' and is a USD ceiling for the whole run (slide 14); a breaker that stops the run is day 5. (8) Catch-up loop for humans: `git checkout <tag> -- <paths>` per step tag (slides 3, 49). Proof to show: tasks.md with all [x] and the quoted pnpm check summary line as the last task; commits in order scenario → red test → green (slide 44); the `Tests N failed | M passed` line from the red run; spec:check counters moving from `specs: 0 · active changes: 0 · archived: 0` to non-zero (slide 42). No Makefile or Stop hook is mentioned on day 3; scripts are package.json scripts (check, spec:check, openspec:pin).
result.verification: Gates (slide 13, 26): `pnpm check` = typecheck → lint → test → spec:check; `pnpm spec:check` = node scripts/spec-check.mjs, runs ONLY the pinned OpenSpec from node_modules (never global) with `OPENSPEC_TELEMETRY=0`, prints one success line `spec:check ok — specs: N · active changes: N · archived: N`, and FAILS if: (a) `validate --all --strict --no-interactive` returns an error (e.g. ## Purpose stub 'TBD - created by archiving change …'); (b) something is archived but `validate --archived` is not green (e.g. '✗ 1 incomplete task (0/1 completed)'); (c) archive exists but openspec/specs/ is empty; (d) a bare `openspec` call reappears in generated skills or /opsx commands. 'Gate ≠ status' (slide 15): a gate is read by a script and refuses with an exit code; three questions for any gate — what exactly does it fail on (list of conditions, not 'if something is wrong'), have you seen it fail at least once on purpose, what does it print when there is nothing to check yet. Empty-tree trap: `pnpm exec openspec validate --all --strict` exits 0 on an empty tree, so the gate prints counters — 'specs: 0 means nothing proven yet' (slides 15, 24, 26). Slide 20 delta file changes/add-price-lookup/specs/pricing/spec.md (sketch, verbatim):
## ADDED Requirements
### Requirement: Model price lookup
The system SHALL return USD-per-token rates for a model id present in data/pricing/models.json.
#### Scenario: Known model
- **WHEN** the model id is "claude-opus-5"
- **THEN** input is 0.000005 and output is 0.000025
#### Scenario: Unpriced model
- **WHEN** the model id is "codex-auto-review"
- **THEN** the result is marked unpriced ("без ціни"), not 0, and no exception is thrown

Rules: SHALL/MUST goes in the requirement line directly under `### Requirement:` (in the heading does not count); every ADDED/MODIFIED requirement needs at least one `#### Scenario:` (four hashes — `### Scenario:` is silently ignored, slide 25 trap 7); requirements in English (Ukrainian text without SHALL fails --strict, slide 25 trap 8); a delta describes the CHANGE, not the whole spec — archive merges it into openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md. Four delta sections (slides 20–21): `## ADDED Requirements` (new), `## MODIFIED Requirements` (copy the WHOLE requirement block with ALL scenarios — a missing scenario still present in specs/ fails `--strict` exit 1 and `archive -y` exit 1 'Aborted. No files were changed.'), `## REMOVED Requirements` (requires `**Reason**:` and `**Migration**:`), `## RENAMED Requirements` (`- FROM: \`### Requirement: Login\`` / `- TO: \`### Requirement: Password login\``). Example archive output: `pnpm exec openspec archive c-evolve -y` → `Totals: + 1, ~ 1, - 1, → 1`. `## Purpose` (slide 24): one sentence 'why this capability exists', written by the agent at propose; if absent in a new capability's delta, archive writes 'TBD - created by archiving change <name>. Update Purpose after archive.' and strict validation then fails — a human reads and rewrites it. config.yaml rule (slides 11, 19): 'Every scenario names concrete input values and the exact expected output, so a test can assert it.' Slide 11 contract table: WHEN id = claude-opus-5 → THEN input 0.000005 · output 0.000025 USD per token; WHEN id = codex-auto-review → THEN marked 'без ціни', not $0 and not an exception. Notation lineage (slide 7): SHALL/MUST — RFC 2119 (1997); Given/When/Then — BDD, Dan North 2006; WHEN … THE SYSTEM SHALL — EARS (Rolls-Royce 2009, used by Kiro). Artifact graph (slide 21): proposal → specs + design → tasks → apply; dependencies are 'enablers, not gates'; `status` only checks that files exist. Mapping to AI-native SDLC playbook (slide 10): proposal.md ≈ intent, delta spec ≈ spec, tasks.md ≈ plan.

Outside a change: trust level 1 ("Assistant") — propose, then wait for a human decision before changing more than one file or running anything that is not on the allow-list in .claude/settings.json.

Definition of done (section named on slides 12–13, 24; content paraphrased from slides 5/12): all tasks.md items [x] · change archived · ## Purpose of the archived spec read by a human · finish with pnpm check output, not the word «готово»
sdd.critique: Slide 9 'Критика SDD — і що з неї беремо': WATERFALL — Kent Beck (via Fowler, 08.01.2026): SDD descriptions assume the whole spec is written before code, as if nothing learned during implementation changes it. REVIEW BURDEN — Böckeler: a small Kiro bug grew into 4 user stories with 16 acceptance criteria; Spec Kit produced so many markdown files she would rather review code. COST (n=1, pre Spec Kit 1.0) — Scott Logic, increment 1: 689 LOC, 2 577 lines of markdown, ≈3.5 h review; author estimates ≈10× faster without SDD. CONTROL AND DRIFT — agents do not follow all instructions (Böckeler); Radar 11.2025 'We may be relearning a bitter lesson'; a prose spec drifts from code unless tests hold it (TDD Buddy). Balance: Böckeler still finds spec-first valuable; Radar Vol. 34 puts Spec Kit and OpenSpec in Assess. What the course takes: ONE small change, not a PRD · scenarios with numbers · a gate with an exit code · tests per scenario so code drift fails a test · archive into specs/ so the spec outlives the task. 'Навіть FAQ OpenSpec: для виправлення одного символу церемонія, найімовірніше, не варта.' Slide 8 levels (Böckeler): spec-first (spec before, for this task) · spec-anchored (kept after, to evolve the feature — the course's reading of OpenSpec, 'у масштабі однієї зміни: сценарій → тест → archive у specs/') · spec-as-source (humans edit only the spec; Tessl Framework, removed from CLI 0.50.3). Slide 17 'How to choose' (instructor's rule): big new product with many roles → Spec Kit or BMAD; team already in Kiro → its specs; small changes in existing code with a CI gate → OpenSpec. Why OpenSpec here: deltas to living specs/ (no need to describe the whole system), the only tool among four with a CLI validator that gives an exit code on spec content (`openspec validate --strict` → exit 1), Node devDependency pinned by lock-file, one init serves Claude Code and Codex, MIT. Slide 16 compares Spec Kit (no exit-code check), Kiro (approval gates/hooks), BMAD (LLM review PASS/CONCERNS/FAIL). Slide 7: Technology Radar Vol. 34 cites SDD as a term that spread before its meaning settled; GitHub: agents are 'literal-minded pair programmers'. Slide 14 token budget: today it is a requirement (number before, honest measurement after), not an enforced breaker.

agentsMd.structure: Day 02 treats AGENTS.md / root CLAUDE.md as the STATIC context layer that is 'Re-injected from disk' after every compaction (slide 18). Cross-tool table (slide 60): 'Статичний контекст: CLAUDE.md → @AGENTS.md | AGENTS.md нативно (Cursor) | AGENTS.md нативно (Codex) — переноситься сам'. Recommended shape: (1) root CLAUDE.md that does `@AGENTS.md` import, so AGENTS.md is tool-portable; (2) a `# Compact instructions` section in CLAUDE.md that names the invariants the summary must keep (slide 23, 38 — 'шар 2'); (3) style rules without `paths:` frontmatter go to the root so they survive compaction (slides 21, 38); (4) invariants that MUST hold are NOT written as rule text at all — they go into a PreToolUse hook (slide 22, 38 — 'шар 3'). Rule of thumb from slide 8: 'Акуратний AGENTS.md не рятує від жодної [причини деградації]; він вирішує лише, що саме займе бюджет.' Slide 20: most important instructions at the START of SKILL.md because truncation keeps the beginning. Reviewer subagent is asked to check code 'проти AGENTS.md' (slide 35), i.e. AGENTS.md is the contract the checker uses.

antiPatterns: Writing an invariant as a 'carefully scoped' path-rule (.claude/rules/*.md with paths:) — it loads into message history and 'compaction summarizes them away with everything else' (slide 21, 36). Course calls this 'інверсія': the narrow rule is less durable than the sloppy root one.

Relying on a rule in CLAUDE.md to guarantee behaviour: ConstraintRot (arXiv 2606.22528) — rule honoured 100% while in window, violated in 30% of episodes after ONE compaction step, 38% if summary dropped it, 0% if it survived (slide 22).

Expecting a skill to self-activate by description after compaction — the skills listing 'is not re-injected after /compact. Only skills you actually invoked get preserved' (slide 20). Name the skill explicitly.

Putting a >5,000-token file in the agent's hands and assuming it 'has' it after compact — it comes back as 'Referenced file' (path only); 'Its rules still reload' but content does not (slides 19, 37).
Fixing the agent a third time in the same spot: 'Третє виправлення — це не наполегливість, це плата за сміття у вікні' → /clear and a better prompt instead (slide 33).

result.staticVsDynamicContext:
Day 02 defines the split by WHAT SURVIVES COMPACTION and by COST ORDER, not by file type. Framework (slide 4, 'Три питання вечора — упорядковані за ціною'): 1 Виміряй (/context, /doctor, /usage) → 2 Не пускай ('Найдешевший токен — той, що не потрапив у вікно: вузький промпт, відкладені схеми MCP, субагент із власним вікном, /btw') → 3 Винеси назовні ('файл на диску, кореневий CLAUDE.md, hook'). 'Порядок не за модою, а за ціною: не завантажити дешевше, ніж ізолювати; ізолювати дешевше, ніж стиснути.'

STATIC (re-injected from disk, survives compact — slide 18 table, verbatim docs): System prompt/output style 'Unchanged; not part of message history'; root CLAUDE.md, unscoped rules, auto memory, plan-mode plan 'Re-injected from disk'. Cross-tool table slide 60 names the layers: Статичний контекст = CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md; Навички = .claude/skills/; Правила за шляхом = .claude/rules/*.md paths:; Межі й дозволи = permissions у settings.json; Динамічний контекст = .mcp.json ${VAR}; Спостережуваність = hooks у settings.json.

DYNAMIC / EPHEMERAL (lives in message history, rewritten by compact — slides 18, 37): path-scoped rules ('Claude Code reloads them as Claude reads files they match'); nested CLAUDE.md; files read ('re-reads up to five, most recently modified first', >5,000 tokens → 'Referenced file' path only); invoked skill bodies ('capped at 5,000 tokens per skill and 25,000 tokens total; oldest dropped first'); context added by hooks ('Summarized with the rest of the conversation'); tool-search results (slide 27: 'живе у повідомленнях — і зникає, щойно компакт дійде до них'). MCP = dynamic ACCESS (slide 2: 'skills як теки, MCP як доступ, hooks як примус'). Hooks = ENFORCEMENT that 'ніколи не жив у вікні' (slide 38).

PROOF EXPECTED (slides 25, 41, 49): 'Виміряти → змінити одне → виміряти знову'; a docs/context-log.md row with three columns — До (numbers from first /context, with model name), Після (same lines after ONE harness change), Доказ поведінки ('що агент зробив або перестав робити: заблокована дія в .agent-log/actions.jsonl, правило, яке він знову цитує, тест, що позеленів'). 'БЕЗ ТРЕТЬОЇ КОЛОНКИ НЕ ЗАРАХОВАНО' (slide 49). Slide 41 checklist for a proof that counts: same prompt word-for-word; fresh session or repeated /compact so the rule explanation is not in recent history; negative control (before the change the same action went through); evidence is 'рядок у .agent-log/actions.jsonl, а не речення в чаті'. The demo's step-05 proof is binary 'знає → не знає → знову знає' on the app-router rule (slide 36).

result.loopEngineering:
Day 02 does not teach code 'to-green' loops per se (that is Day 03/04 territory); its loop is the MEASUREMENT loop and it is explicit about what counts as proof of a loop in the capstone.

1. The method (slide 25, 'Шість кроків, один цикл'): 'Виміряти → змінити одне → виміряти знову … крок, у якому немає другого виміру, — це не важіль, а віра.' Each demo step is a git tag (step-01-measure … step-06-enforce) with a rollback `git checkout step-0N-… -- <paths>` (slides 25, 53).

2. Homework loop in your own repo (slide 49), one session, three measurements:
   › /context            # record Free space + MCP tools — 'до'
   # change EXACTLY ONE thing in the harness
   › /context            # same lines — 'після'
   $ claude              # fresh session
   › the same prompt, word for word
   $ node scripts/agent-log-summary.mjs
   → one row in docs/context-log.md with columns До / Після / Доказ поведінки.

3. Green gate inside the loop (slide 30): `pnpm check  # typecheck + lint + test` → '✓ typecheck · ✓ lint · ✓ tests passed' then `git add -A && git commit -m "03 design cost"`. Pre-flight (slide 24): `claude --version → 2.1.261+`, `echo $ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH → порожньо`, `pnpm check → зелений`, 'журнал засіяний'.

4. Behavioural loop (slide 38): `pnpm agent:log` baseline → change one layer → `/compact` → identical prompt → `pnpm agent:log` again, expect +1 blocked row.

5. Session-relay loop (slide 39): every session OPENS by reading docs/session-notes.md ('Прочитай docs/session-notes.md і продовжуй') and CLOSES by updating it; `/clear день02-контекст` names the conversation for /resume; `/btw` for side questions that must not cost the window ('ні питання, ні відповідь не входять в історію', but no tools).

6. Which lever first (slides 33, 43): '/clear — коштує нічого · /compact — сам по собі великий запит … · /rewind — обрізає до префікса, який уже в кеші'; '/rewind, а не /compact' to drop a bad branch (slide 28); 'Не пускати перемагає стиснути потім' (LOCA-bench, slide 43).

7. What the capstone rubric wants as LOOP PROOF (slide 47, verbatim): 'команда циклу і вивід одного прогону: скільки ітерацій, на чому спинився' — i.e. commit the loop command (script / Makefile target) AND the captured output of one run showing iteration count and stop reason. A sentence like «Перевірив, що все працює» is explicitly listed as 'ТАК ВИГЛЯДАЄ СЛОВО' (not proof).

No Stop hook, Makefile or iteration-log format is defined in Day 02.

result.makerChecker:
Day 02 frames the subagent strictly as CONTEXT ISOLATION ('Сьогодні субагент з'являється виключно як ізоляція контексту. Усе інше про кількох агентів — заняття 4', slide 34), but step-04 is a reviewer and the capstone rubric names 'maker ≠ checker — окремий агент або прохід на рев'ю' (slide 46).

Definition file (slide 35, tag step-04-isolate, fallback `git checkout step-04-isolate -- .claude/agents`):
  $ cat .claude/agents/design-reviewer.md
  name: design-reviewer        # обов'язкові лише name і description
  description: …
  tools: —  allowlist · model: — задаємо явно
Invocation prompt (verbatim): '@agent-design-reviewer перевір components/UsageMeter.tsx проти AGENTS.md; поверни лише список знайдених розбіжностей і рішення, які довелось прийняти'. Key design choice: the reviewer checks AGAINST AGENTS.md (the contract) and is told to return ONLY the discrepancy list + decisions, so the main window gets a summary not a transcript.

How output is captured: 'У вікно повернувся лише підсумок і невеликий метадата-трейлер — не транскрипт'; full transcript on disk: `ls -lS ~/.claude/projects/*course-day02/*/subagents/agent-*.jsonl | head -3` — 'великий транскрипт на диску ↔ мала дельта у вашому вікні'. Measure with /context before/after and /usage. The transcript file 'при компакті головної розмови не чіпається'.

What the subagent sees (slide 34): no conversation history, no files the main session read, no auto memory; BUT loads the whole CLAUDE.md hierarchy + git status snapshot + skills named in its `skills` field in full. Built-in Explore and Plan skip CLAUDE.md/git status. Its window is set by ITS model; first request does not hit the parent cache; subagents get a 5-minute cache TTL even on subscription. /subtask and /fork inherit the whole conversation ('ізолюють вивід, але не вхід'). Agent teams ≈ 7× tokens in plan mode.

Capstone proof format (slide 47): 'вивід субагента-рецензента і що саме він знайшов' — commit the reviewer's returned list and link it. Caveat for the checker (slide 14): long-context reviewers miss issues 2–30× more; keep the review pass fresh and scoped.

otherPractices: Compaction is two-stage (slide 16): stage 1 silently drops old tool outputs ('вивід вашого pnpm check просто більше не у вікні'), stage 2 summarises; 'detailed instructions from early in the conversation may be lost'. Design: never rely on an early-chat instruction.
Compact trigger is a token count per model, not a published % (slide 17): 200K-window models compact at ~200K; native 1M (Sonnet 5, Fable, Opus 4.7+) ≈ 967K. Only trust the live /context number.
After compact only the 5 most-recently-modified files are re-read; >5,000-token files return as 'Referenced file' (slides 19, 37). Keep key files small, or re-read explicitly after /compact.
Skill bodies re-injected capped 5,000/skill, 25,000 total, truncation keeps the file START → put critical instructions at the top of SKILL.md and invoke skills by name after compact (slide 20).
Steer compaction: '/compact focus on the auth bug fix'; '/rewind → Summarize from here / Summarize up to here'; CLAUDE.md '# Compact instructions' (slide 23).

Cost of levers (slides 23, 33): /clear free; /compact is itself a large request (reads the whole conversation); /rewind truncates to an already-cached prefix. Drop a bad branch with /rewind, not /compact.
Operational rule (slide 33): corrected the agent more than twice in the same place → /clear + better prompt, not a third fix.
Tool output, not your code, fills the window (slide 28): same answer cost 10 tool calls vs 1 with a filter hook. Write-to-file for big outputs is already harness behaviour (slide 29).
Place generated components outside path-rule globs when you want a clean measurement (slide 30: components/ not app/, because re-read files under app/ would reload the rule).

Measure each harness change: /context before, /context after, same prompt in a fresh session, scripts/agent-log-summary.mjs (slide 49). Six-row scoreboard format (slide 40): Крок·тег | Прилад | Що саме змінилось | Одиниця виміру.

Pre-flight before a session (slide 24): claude --version 2.1.261+; echo $ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH empty; pnpm check green; journal seeded; git tags in place. Cache TTL: 1h on subscription, 5 min on usage credits and for subagents.
/context numbers are an estimate since v2.1.261 (local count when token-counting API unavailable); /doctor is a bundled skill, CLAUDE.md-trim check needs v2.1.206+ (slide 26).

Honesty about numbers (slides 44, 54): no published figure for subagent savings, compact-vs-no-compact delta, share of sessions reaching compact, or a degradation curve — 'Порожня клітинка — теж результат'. Cite primary sources; label own measurements with machine/model/date.

Cross-tool portability (slides 55–60): CLAUDE.md→@AGENTS.md, .claude/skills/ port as-is; .claude/rules paths: ↔ .cursor/rules/*.mdc globs (comma string, .mdc not .md); permissions ↔ .cursor/permissions.json (terminalAllowlist, mcpAllowlist, autoRun; file only active when Run Mode enabled; replaces UI list); hooks need an adapter; exit 2 blocks in both tools.

Slide 31/54 Figma MCP: Starter 20 calls/month, paid View/Collab 6/month; one get_design_context measured at 351,378 tokens vs 25,000 cap — pick smaller nodes, use get_metadata first. - /opsx:propose <name-or-description>  (skill openspec-propose) - "Propose a new change - create it and generate all artifacts in one step". Runs `openspec context --json`, derives kebab-case name, `openspec new change "<name>"`, then for each artifact `openspec instructions <artifact> --change "<name>" --json` and writes proposal.md -> specs/<cap>/spec.md -> design.md -> tasks.md, re-checking `openspec status --change "<name>" --json`. PLANNING ONLY: it explicitly refuses to touch project code and stops after artifacts; you must then run /opsx:apply in a new message.
- /opsx:explore [topic]  (openspec-explore) - "Enter explore mode - think through ideas, investigate problems, clarify requirements". Read-only thinking partner; optional before propose.
- /opsx:apply [change-name]  (openspec-apply-change) - "Implement tasks from an OpenSpec change". This IS the "implement" step (there is no /opsx:implement). Runs `openspec status --change X --json` and `openspec instructions apply --change X --json`, works through tasks.md, flips `- [ ]` to `- [x]` immediately after each task passes its verification, pauses on blockers. Auto-selects the change if only one is active.
- /opsx:update [change-name]  (openspec-update-change) - "Update a change - revise existing planning artifacts and keep them coherent". Drafts edits to proposal/specs/design/tasks, applies after your confirmation, never edits code. (Not to be confused with CLI `openspec update`, which regenerates .claude/ files.)
- /opsx:sync [change-name]  (openspec-sync-specs) - "Sync delta specs from a change to main specs". AGENT-DRIVEN merge: the agent reads each delta and edits openspec/specs/<cap>/spec.md directly (can add one scenario without rewriting the requirement), creates missing main specs from ADDED, then runs `openspec validate --specs`. Use when you want main specs updated before/without archiving.
- /opsx:archive [change-name]  (openspec-archive-change) - "Archive a completed change". Checks `openspec status --change X --json` completeness and task progress, loads `openspec instructions archive --change X --json` (context + operationGuidance), offers to run the /opsx:sync workflow inline for unsynced deltas (in 1.13.1 it delegates to the sync skill; 1.14.0 merges itself), then moves the change dir to openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/ (same naming rule as the CLI). Parser facts (dist/core/parsers + validation, 1.13.1): headings are matched case-insensitively; section headers are `##`, requirements `### Requirement: <name>`, scenarios MUST be `#### Scenario: <name>` (exactly 4 hashes - 3 hashes or bullet-only scenarios "fail silently" / are not counted); scenario bodies are bullet lines `- **WHEN** ...` / `- **THEN** ...` (and `- **AND** ...`, `- **GIVEN**` accepted as free text); requirement body SHOULD contain the English keyword SHALL or MUST (missing keyword = WARNING, which FAILS under --strict); every ADDED/MODIFIED requirement needs >= 1 scenario (ERROR); requirement text > 500 chars = INFO; delta spec must live at specs/<capability-path>/spec.md (a file at specs/spec.md is an ERROR and ignored by archive); capability path segments kebab-case.

# product-catalog Specification

Provides a single read-only catalog that aggregates products from several integrated organic shops.

## Requirements

The system SHALL return a list of products aggregated from all integrated shops, each with name, price, image and source shop.

#### Scenario: Catalog is requested

- **THEN** the response is HTTP 200 with a JSON array of products from every integrated shop

D) All delta section forms (full template from the shipped sync skill):

## ADDED Requirements          # new requirements; appended to main spec
## MODIFIED Requirements       # header must match an existing `### Requirement:` name (whitespace-insensitive); MUST carry the FULL block (text + every surviving scenario) - a MODIFIED that drops a scenario the main spec has is rejected by validate and archive ("scenario-loss guard"); the whole block is replaced
## REMOVED Requirements        # only the header is needed to delete: `### Requirement: Deprecated Feature`; schema instruction says also add `**Reason**: ...` and `**Migration**: ...` lines (good practice; validator only parses names - enforcement unconfirmed)
## RENAMED Requirements        # bullet pairs: `- FROM: `### Requirement: Old Name`` then `- TO: `### Requirement: New Name``; must be complete pairs

Delta validation rules (validate / --strict): >= 1 delta across the change unless .openspec.yaml has skip_specs: true; no duplicate requirement names within a section; no cross-section conflicts (same name in ADDED+REMOVED, MODIFIED+ADDED, MODIFIED+REMOVED, RENAMED+REMOVED, RENAMED TO vs ADDED); MODIFIED must use the new name after a RENAME; delta description (first requirement sentence) >= 10 chars (WARNING); ADDED/MODIFIED section with zero parsed requirements (WARNING); > 10 deltas per change ("Consider splitting", level unconfirmed); requirements written outside any delta section are warned with line numbers and ignored. `--strict` = valid only when errors == 0 AND warnings == 0 (dist/core/validation/validator.js createReport). Delta specs must be at openspec/changes/<id>/specs/<capability-path>/spec.md. A file at specs/spec.md (no capability folder) is an ERROR and is ignored by apply/archive.

`--strict` turns every WARNING into a failure: Purpose < 50 chars or a TBD/TODO placeholder, requirement body without SHALL/MUST, delta description < 10 chars, ADDED/MODIFIED section with no parsed requirement, tasks file without checkboxes. If a new-capability delta has no Purpose, archive writes the placeholder 'TBD - created by archiving change <name>. Update Purpose after archive.' which then fails --strict as a placeholder.

MODIFIED must contain the ENTIRE requirement block (text + all existing scenarios + new ones). Archive replaces the whole block by header name; a MODIFIED that omits a scenario present in the main spec is rejected ('scenario-loss guard'). Header text must match the main spec exactly (whitespace-insensitive). If you only add new concerns, use ADDED instead.
`/opsx:propose` is planning-only - it will not write code even if asked; implementation is `/opsx:apply <change>` in a NEW message. There is no /opsx:implement.

# Organic Catalog — project rules

Shop aggregator: 10 products from each of 2 organic shops in one catalog, plus a basket (add, update qty, delete).
Next.js 16 App Router — frontend and API routes in one repo; TypeScript strict; Vitest; pnpm only.

## Commands (pnpm only — never npm or yarn)
- pnpm check      — typecheck + lint + test + spec:check; run it before "done"
- pnpm typecheck  = next typegen && tsc --noEmit · pnpm lint = eslint (next lint no longer exists)
- pnpm test       = vitest run · pnpm spec:check = node scripts/spec-check.mjs
- pnpm agent:log  — summary of .agent-log/actions.jsonl · pnpm hooks:selftest — prove hooks without an agent
- OpenSpec CLI only as `pnpm exec openspec` (pinned devDependency), never a bare `openspec`

## Trust level
- Inside an OpenSpec change (openspec/changes/<id>/): trust level 3 ("Agent") — implement that change's
  tasks.md end to end, edit the files it needs, run allow-listed commands, finish with pnpm check output.
- Outside a change: trust level 1 ("Assistant") — propose, then wait for a human decision before changing
  more than one file or running anything not on the allow-list in .claude/settings.json.
- Left the change's scope → back to level 1, without discussion.

## OpenSpec change cycle
- /opsx:propose writes proposal, delta specs, tasks — zero code; gate: pnpm spec:check; then STOP and wait
  for a human to read the scenarios before /opsx:apply.
- /opsx:apply: task 1 = scenario tests shown RED (quote the "Tests N failed | M passed" line), then implement
  rule by rule until pnpm check is green; tick "- [x]" only after that task's own verification passed.
- /opsx:archive (or pnpm exec openspec archive <id> --yes); gate: pnpm spec:check; a human reads ## Purpose.
- Specs in English; SHALL/MUST in the line under "### Requirement:"; "#### Scenario:" (four hashes) with
  concrete input values and the exact expected output, so a test can assert it.

## Definition of done
- Evidence, not claims: the command you ran + exit code or summary line. "Done", "fixed", "should work" are not evidence.
- A change is done when every tasks.md item is [x] · the change is archived · ## Purpose was read by a human ·
  the reply ends with pnpm check output, not the word "done".
- Mark a feature complete only after end-to-end verification confirms it works, not when the code is written.

## Next.js 16 rules
- await params / searchParams / cookies() / headers(); proxy.ts, not middleware.ts; caching is opt-in.
- Unsure about a Next API: read node_modules/next/dist/docs/ or query Context7 (mcp__context7__query-docs).
  A correct answer "from memory" is not proof of the call.

## Conventions
- lib/ — pure functions with a Vitest test beside the module; route handlers thin; async Server Components are not unit-tested.
- Shop data comes only from committed fixtures in fixtures/shops/; tests never touch the network.
  The correct counts and prices live in fixtures/shops/README.md — the agent does not decide which number is right.
- UI copy Ukrainian; code, specs and commits English. Conventional commits; no Claude attribution lines in commits.

## Observability
- Hooks append .agent-log/actions.jsonl (PreToolUse = proposed, PostToolUse = executed). Never edit .agent-log/
  or .claude/hooks/; summarise with pnpm agent:log — never parse the JSONL by hand.

## Boundaries
- Ask first: new dependencies, next.config.ts, .claude/settings.json, .mcp.json, openspec/config.yaml.
- Never: touch .env*, delete or weaken tests, disable lint, read the real ~/.claude, git push --force.

**What the course showed** — Day 01: the loop is `pnpm check` as the agent's self-verification ("дайте агенту спосіб перевірити себе", D1 s24/46) and the task format Мета · Критерій · Межі · Бюджет with an explicit termination sign ("Готово, коли pnpm check і pnpm build зелені. Не додавай залежностей.", D1 s49). Day 02: the measurement loop (measure → change one thing → measure again, D2 s25) and the rubric line for loop proof: "команда циклу і вивід одного прогону: скільки ітерацій, на чому спинився" (D2 s47). Day 03: "Агент ітерує, доки гейт не зелений, — а не доки не скаже «готово»" (D3 s13) inside /opsx:apply, with `claude -p` runs measured via their `result` events and `--max-budget-usd` (print mode only, D3 s14). **No loop script, Makefile or Stop hook was shown on Days 01–03** (Day 05 topic). The script below is therefore **course silent — proposed**, built from those three pieces: a fresh `claude -p` session per iteration (D2 s33 "a clean session with a better prompt almost always outperforms a long session"), the same prompt word for word (D2 s41), the gate's exit code as the only stop condition, a USD ceiling, and a committed run log.

### 4.1 scripts/loop.mjs (`pnpm loop -- --change organic-catalog-mvp`)

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// scripts/loop.mjs — run the agent until `pnpm check` is green, with an iteration log.
// Usage: node scripts/loop.mjs --change <id> [--max-iter 5] [--budget-usd 3] [--prompt-file docs/loop-prompt.md]
// Stop reasons: green | max-iter | budget | no-progress
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { appendFileSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';

const arg = (k, d) => { const i = process.argv.indexOf(k); return i > -1 ? process.argv[i + 1] : d; };
const change = arg('--change');
const maxIter = Number(arg('--max-iter', 5));
const budget = Number(arg('--budget-usd', 3));
const promptFile = arg('--prompt-file', 'docs/loop-prompt.md');
if (!change) { console.error('usage: node scripts/loop.mjs --change <id>'); process.exit(2); }

const ts = new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, '-');
mkdirSync('docs/loop-runs', { recursive: true });
mkdirSync('.agent-log', { recursive: true });
const runLog = `docs/loop-runs/${ts}-${change}.md`;
const basePrompt = readFileSync(promptFile, 'utf8').replaceAll('{{change}}', change);
const ALLOWED = [
  'Read', 'Edit', 'Write', 'Bash(pnpm check)', 'Bash(pnpm test *)', 'Bash(pnpm typecheck)',
  'Bash(pnpm lint)', 'Bash(pnpm spec:check)', 'Bash(pnpm exec openspec *)', 'Bash(git diff *)', 'Bash(git status *)',
].join(',');

const gate = () => {
  const g = spawnSync('pnpm', ['check'], { encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 64e6 });
  const tail = `${g.stdout ?? ''}${g.stderr ?? ''}`.split('\n').slice(-40).join('\n');
  return { status: g.status ?? 1, tail };
};

writeFileSync(runLog, `# loop run ${ts} — change ${change}\n\nbudget: $${budget} · max-iter: ${maxIter}\n\n`);
let spent = 0, iterations = 0, lastTail = '', stop = 'max-iter';

for (let i = 1; i <= maxIter; i++) {
  const g = gate();
  appendFileSync(runLog, `## iteration ${i}\n\n\`\`\`\n$ pnpm check   # exit ${g.status}\n${g.tail}\n\`\`\`\n\n`);
  if (g.status === 0) { stop = 'green'; break; }
  if (g.tail === lastTail) { stop = 'no-progress'; break; }   // same failure twice → stop, a human looks
  lastTail = g.tail;
  iterations = i;

  const prompt = `${basePrompt}\n\nLast \`pnpm check\` output (exit ${g.status}):\n\`\`\`\n${g.tail}\n\`\`\``;
  const a = spawnSync('claude', [
    '-p', prompt, '--permission-mode', 'acceptEdits', '--output-format', 'json',
    '--max-budget-usd', String(Math.max(0.05, budget - spent).toFixed(2)),
    '--allowedTools', ALLOWED,
  ], { encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 64e6 });

  let cost = 0, outTokens = 0, result = '';
  try {
    const j = JSON.parse(a.stdout);                     // `result` event of claude -p (D3 s14/41)
    cost = Number(j.total_cost_usd ?? 0);
    outTokens = Number(j.usage?.output_tokens ?? 0);
    result = String(j.result ?? '');
  } catch { result = (a.stdout ?? '').slice(-2000); }
  spent += cost;

  appendFileSync(runLog, `agent exit ${a.status} · cost $${cost.toFixed(2)} · output tokens ${outTokens} · spent $${spent.toFixed(2)}\n\n> ${result.split('\n').slice(0, 12).join('\n> ')}\n\n`);
  appendFileSync('.agent-log/loop.jsonl', JSON.stringify({ ts: new Date().toISOString(), change, iteration: i, gateExit: g.status, cost, outTokens, spent }) + '\n');
  if (spent >= budget) { stop = 'budget'; break; }
}

const final = gate();
const summary = `loop: change=${change} iterations=${iterations} stopped=${stop} final pnpm check exit=${final.status} spent=$${spent.toFixed(2)}`;
appendFileSync(runLog, `\n**${summary}**\n`);
console.log(summary);
process.exit(final.status === 0 ? 0 : 1);
```

# Spec Delta

## Purpose
Lets a user collect catalog products into a basket and change or remove its lines before checkout.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Add a product to the basket
`POST /api/basket` with `{ productId, qty }` SHALL create a basket line and return HTTP 201 with `{ id, productId, qty }`; a second POST for the same productId MUST increase qty of the existing line instead of creating a second one.

#### Scenario: Product added twice
- **WHEN** `POST /api/basket` is sent with `{ "productId": "karashynyard:«slug-1»", "qty": 1 }` and then again with `qty: 2`
- **THEN** `GET /api/basket` returns one line with `qty: 3`

#### Scenario: Unknown product
- **WHEN** `POST /api/basket` is sent with `{ "productId": "nope:x", "qty": 1 }`
- **THEN** the response is HTTP 404 with `{ "error": "product not found" }`

### Requirement: Update a basket line quantity
`PATCH /api/basket/:id` with `{ qty }` SHALL set the line quantity and return HTTP 200 with the line; qty MUST be an integer ≥ 1, otherwise HTTP 400; an unknown id returns HTTP 404.

#### Scenario: Quantity changed
- **WHEN** a line `{ id: "L1", qty: 3 }` exists and `PATCH /api/basket/L1` is sent with `{ "qty": 5 }`
- **THEN** the response is HTTP 200 with `{ "id": "L1", "qty": 5 }`

#### Scenario: Invalid quantity
- **WHEN** `PATCH /api/basket/L1` is sent with `{ "qty": 0 }`
- **THEN** the response is HTTP 400 with `{ "error": "qty must be an integer >= 1" }`

### Requirement: Delete a basket line
`DELETE /api/basket/:id` SHALL remove the line and return HTTP 204; an unknown id returns HTTP 404.

#### Scenario: Line deleted
- **WHEN** a line `L1` exists and `DELETE /api/basket/L1` is sent
- **THEN** the response is HTTP 204 and `GET /api/basket` no longer contains `L1`

### Requirement: Basket total
`GET /api/basket` SHALL return `{ items, totalKop }` where totalKop is the sum of `priceKop × qty` over priced lines.

#### Scenario: Total of two lines
- **WHEN** the basket holds `{ productId: A (priceKop 12500), qty: 2 }` and `{ productId: B (priceKop 8000), qty: 1 }`
- **THEN** `GET /api/basket` returns `totalKop: 33000`
